title: Thanksgiving Address to Origen
author: Gregory Thaumaturgus
edition: Opera omnia, Greek and Latin (Paris, 1622): Latin column for the opening section, Greek column for the rest
blurb: Gregory's farewell speech to his teacher Origen: how a pagan boy bound for law school in Berytus was led to Caesarea, how Origen taught him logic, natural science, ethics and the reading of Scripture, and his grief at leaving. A fresh English translation of the whole address.
era_note: Delivered at Caesarea in Palestine as Gregory prepared to return home after studying under Origen. Jerome (Lives of Illustrious Men 65) names the address.
first_english_note: Prior English exists (Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. 6, Salmond, public domain); this is a fresh English translation of the whole address.

text_history.method: The opening section (to the point where Gregory turns to his subject) was translated from the Latin column of the Opera omnia print (Paris, 1622). Everything after it, to the closing prayer, was translated from that print's Greek column, read from the page images; the facing Latin was used to settle damaged or abbreviated words. Where the print is hard to construe, a few readings follow Koetschau's edition (1894); each one is named in the translator notes. The older Ante-Nicene Fathers English was used only as a sense check for the opening section.

joins.note: Translated from the Latin column; the Greek of this opening was not used. Long-s and column joins expanded (ductu; nec aut scripsi; historiamve; arte nostra); the editor's argument and notes left out.

Abbreviated words read from the page images and the facing Latin: 'father' (πατρός), 'toward our sister' (πρὸς τὴν ἀδελφήν), 'through the whole of this life' (διὰ παντός), 'handing over his charge' (τὴν οἰκονομίαν παραδιδούς), 'with difficulty' (δυσχερῶς).
The print's doubtful participle (βλέψαν) is rendered with Koetschau's reading βλάψαν ('without doing it any harm').
The print runs one sentence across the break; it is translated once, at the start of section 8, where Koetschau begins chapter 8.
